summary: A three-person studio workspace: the founder's assistant handles mail, calendar and the Monday brief; a Clients Space runs status drafts, call-note tasks and launch QA; a Members only Finance Space prepares invoices and reminders; a New business Space drafts proposals, inquiry replies and LinkedIn posts. Everything starts paused and nothing is sent without approval.

talk.why: No sign of voice use in the evidence; can be switched on later.

members.title: Designer
members.responsibilities: Brand and UI design in Figma, icons

spaces.name: Clients
spaces.purpose: Client website projects from kick-off to launch: weekly status, tasks from calls, design and build hand-offs, launch QA and site health.
spaces.why: Most repeated work is per client project and shared by all three people.

spaces.name: Finance
spaces.purpose: Monthly invoice lines from time tracking, overdue invoices and reminders. Money matters stay with the founder.
spaces.why: Invoicing repeats monthly and needs to stay private.

spaces.name: New business
spaces.purpose: Website inquiries, discovery calls, proposals, case studies and LinkedIn posts.
spaces.why: Proposals, inquiries and posts share the same voice, prices and pipeline.

agents.name: Assistant
agents.instructions:
You work for the founder of a three-person brand and web studio. Keep answers short. Write German to clients and English internally.

Every Monday prepare the week: calls that need preparation, deadlines, open threads waiting on a reply, and three suggested priorities. During the week help with mail and the calendar: draft replies, find slots, summarise threads. Never send a mail or accept an invitation without asking first.

Follow the Brand voice in Company knowledge for anything a client reads.
agents.why: Personal mail, calendar and the Monday brief.

agents.name: Clients
agents.instructions:
You run the studio's client projects. Each client has a Project in this Space.

After a call, when notes are posted or added to Notion, create tasks in Notion with an owner (founder, designer or developer) and a due date, then post the list in the chat.

On Fridays draft one status update per active project from the week's Notion tasks, call notes and Slack threads. Use the Weekly status update template and the Brand voice; German, at most 120 words; done, next, what we need from the client. Post drafts in the chat; never send them.

Ask Launch QA for launch checks and site problems.
agents.why: Coordinates status drafts and call-note tasks for every client.

agents.name: Launch QA
agents.instructions:
You check client websites before launch and every Monday. Follow the launch QA skill and the Website launch checklist: speed scores above 90, German alt texts, broken links, meta titles and descriptions, favicon, 404 page, redirects from old URLs, cookie banner, Search Console.

For launch checks post what needs fixing, most important first, and a short client summary as a draft. For the Monday health check of all live sites (links, SSL expiry, speed) stay quiet when everything is fine and post only problems.

Use the browser to look at sites; never submit forms or change a site.
agents.why: Launch checks and the Monday site check follow the same checklist every time.

agents.name: Finance
agents.instructions: You prepare the studio's invoicing. On the first working day of the month read last month's hours from Toggl Track and make one invoice line per client project at the day rate in Services and prices. Flag entries without a project. Then list invoices unpaid for more than 14 days and draft a polite German reminder for each in the billing inbox. Post the lines as a table the founder can paste into the invoicing tool. You never send mails, book invoices or move money.
agents.why: Monthly invoicing and reminders, kept private.

agents.name: New business
agents.instructions:
You look after new business. For each new project inquiry in the contact inbox, draft a reply following Inquiry replies (thank them, two lines on how we work, the booking link) and post a one-line summary in the chat. Ignore newsletters and tool mails.

On Fridays draft two LinkedIn posts from launches and case studies of the past two weeks, each with three alternative hooks, in the Brand voice. Ask the Proposal writer for proposals. Never send or post anything yourself.
agents.why: Inquiries and posts share the studio's voice and pipeline.

agents.name: Proposal writer
agents.instructions: You turn discovery-call notes into proposals. Follow the proposal skill and the Proposal structure: goals, scope, timeline, price, next steps. Prices come from Services and prices; split design and build; always offer the maintenance retainer. Write German unless asked; add an English scope section when the client has an English-speaking co-founder or asks for it. Deliver a Word document for review. Ask one question when budget or deadline is missing instead of guessing.
agents.why: Eleven proposals in three months with the same structure and the same follow-ups.

knowledge.title: Brand voice
knowledge.content_md:
# Brand voice

- Warm, clear, concrete. Short sentences.
- No buzzwords: innovative, leading, solutions, synergy.
- German for clients unless they write in English; English internally.
- Say what we did and what it changed, with one number when there is one.
- Sign client mails as the studio.
knowledge.why: The voice rules are pasted into prompts again and again.

knowledge.title: Services and prices
knowledge.content_md:
# Services and prices

- Day rate: 850 EUR net.
- Typical website project: 6–10k EUR, split into design and build.
- Always offer a maintenance retainer after launch.

Check with the founder before quoting anything outside these ranges.
knowledge.why: Proposals and invoices use the same rate every time.

knowledge.title: Client onboarding
knowledge.content_md:
# Client onboarding

1. Kick-off call
2. Shared Notion page
3. Slack Connect channel
4. Collect logo, photos and texts
5. Time-tracking project
knowledge.why: An existing process the agents should follow for new clients.

knowledge.title: Weekly status update
knowledge.content_md:
# Weekly status update

Hallo {Name},

kurzes Update zu {Projekt}:
- Erledigt:
- Als Nächstes:
- Wir brauchen von euch:

Viele Grüße
Studio Nordlicht

At most 120 words. Add the staging link when there is one.
knowledge.why: The template behind every Friday update.

knowledge.title: Website launch checklist
knowledge.content_md:
# Website launch checklist

- Speed scores above 90
- Alt texts in German
- 404 page
- Favicon
- Meta titles and descriptions
- Redirects from old URLs
- Cookie banner
- Search Console set up
knowledge.why: The same eight checks before every launch.

knowledge.title: Invoicing
knowledge.content_md:
# Invoicing

- First working day of the month.
- Hours from the time-tracking export, one line per client project.
- Day rate from Services and prices.
- Reminders after 14 days, polite, in German.
- The founder books and sends invoices.
knowledge.why: The monthly routine, written down once.

knowledge.title: Proposal structure
knowledge.content_md:
# Proposal structure

1. Goals — what the client wants to achieve
2. Scope — pages, features, design and build
3. Timeline — phases and launch date
4. Price — day rate, design and build split, maintenance retainer
5. Next steps — call, signature, kick-off
knowledge.why: Every proposal follows these five parts.

knowledge.title: Inquiry replies
knowledge.content_md:
# Inquiry replies

- Thank them and repeat what they asked for in one line.
- Two lines on how we work: discovery call, proposal, design, build, launch.
- Booking link for a 30-minute call: <add your booking link>.
- German unless they wrote in English. Sign as the studio.
knowledge.why: Ten inquiry replies with the same shape.

knowledge.title: LinkedIn ideas
knowledge.content_md:
# LinkedIn ideas

- Launch stories: problem, what we built, one result
- Before and after of a redesign
- How we price websites
knowledge.why: Gives the Friday drafts a starting list.

skills.name: proposal-from-call-notes
skills.description: Turn discovery-call notes into a studio proposal (goals, scope, timeline, price, next steps). Use for every new website or brand project inquiry after a call.

files.content:
---
name: proposal-from-call-notes
description: Turn discovery-call notes into a studio proposal (goals, scope, timeline, price, next steps). Use for every new website or brand project inquiry after a call.
---

# Proposal from call notes

1. Read the notes. If budget, deadline or page count is missing, ask one question.
2. Goals: two or three sentences in the client's words.
3. Scope: pages and features; split design and build.
4. Timeline: phases with weeks; launch date.
5. Price: days × day rate from Services and prices, design and build separately, then the maintenance retainer as an option.
6. Next steps: call to discuss, signature, kick-off date.
7. German by default; add an English scope section when asked.
8. Deliver a Word document and a three-line summary in the chat.

skills.why: The same steps in eleven proposals.

skills.name: launch-qa
skills.description: Check a client website before launch against the studio's checklist and write the fix list and a client summary. Use before every launch and for site problems.

files.content:
---
name: launch-qa
description: Check a client website before launch against the studio's checklist and write the fix list and a client summary. Use before every launch and for site problems.
---

# Launch QA

1. Open the staging or live address in the browser.
2. Run a speed test for mobile and desktop; note scores below 90.
3. Check every page for missing or English alt texts, broken links, missing meta titles and descriptions.
4. Check favicon, 404 page, cookie banner and redirects from the old site.
5. Check Search Console access.
6. Post the fixes, most important first, with the page for each.
7. Draft a five-line summary for the client in German.

skills.why: Three launches, the same checklist each time.

scheduled_tasks.title: Friday client status drafts
scheduled_tasks.instruction: For each active client Project, read this week's Notion tasks and call notes and the project's Slack threads. Draft one status update per client with the Weekly status update template and the Brand voice: German, at most 120 words, done / next / what we need. Post all drafts here, one message per client. Do not send anything. If a project had no activity, say so in one line.
scheduled_tasks.why: Replaces the Friday hour of writing status mails.

scheduled_tasks.title: Monday brief
scheduled_tasks.instruction: Read this week's calendar and the last week's unanswered mail. Write a short brief: calls that need preparation (with one line of context each), deadlines, threads waiting on a reply, and three suggested priorities for the week. Keep it under 200 words.

scheduled_tasks.title: Invoice lines and reminders
scheduled_tasks.instruction: Act only on the first working day of the month; on any other day end without a message. Then: read last month's hours from Toggl Track, group them per client project, and make invoice lines at the day rate from Services and prices. Flag entries without a project. List invoices unpaid for more than 14 days and draft a polite German reminder for each in the billing inbox. Post the invoice lines as a table and the list of reminder drafts here.

timing.human: Weekdays at 9:00, acts only on the first working day

scheduled_tasks.why: The monthly invoicing block and the reminders, prepared before you start.

scheduled_tasks.title: Monday site health check
scheduled_tasks.instruction: Check every live client site listed in the Clients Space for broken links, SSL certificates expiring within 30 days, and mobile speed scores below 80. Post only problems, one line each with the site and what to fix. If everything is fine, end without a message.

scheduled_tasks.title: Friday LinkedIn drafts
scheduled_tasks.instruction: Look at launches and case studies from the past two weeks in Notion and in this Space. Draft two LinkedIn posts (at most 120 words each): the client's problem, what we built, one result. Give three alternative opening hooks for each. Use the Brand voice and LinkedIn ideas. Post them here; never post to LinkedIn.
scheduled_tasks.why: Drafts ready for the Friday content block.

checks.title: New website inquiries
checks.reads: new e-mails to the studio's contact inbox
checks.instruction: If the mail is a new project inquiry, draft a reply following Inquiry replies and post a one-line summary (what they want, budget if stated). Skip newsletters, invoices and tool notifications.
checks.why: Inquiries get a ready reply within minutes.

checks.title: New call notes to tasks
checks.reads: new pages in the call notes database
checks.instruction: For each new call note, create Notion tasks with owner and due date and post the list in the client's Project.
checks.why: No more copying action items by hand.

event_automations.title: Instant reply draft for inquiries
event_automations.instruction: Same as the inquiry check, the moment the mail arrives.
event_automations.why: Would be faster than a 15-minute check once instant triggers exist.

mac_app.why: Launch QA uses the agent's browser, and proposals and invoice tables are documents made on the Mac.

cloud_computer.why: Optional: lets the Monday 7:00 site check run while the Mac is still closed.

manual_steps.title: Choose how the workspace is paid for
manual_steps.why: Subscriptions uses each person's ChatGPT plan; API keys uses workspace keys with a monthly budget.

manual_steps.title: Confirm the studio has a shared contact inbox
manual_steps.why: The inquiry check needs it; without one, skip the check and let the assistant help.

manual_steps.title: Look for your invoicing tool in Add app
manual_steps.why: If it is there, the Finance manager can read open invoices directly; otherwise lines arrive as a table.

manual_steps.title: Add the list of live client sites
manual_steps.why: The Monday check needs the addresses.
